subject: DPA clarifications - Arcadia Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diane Rogers <diane.rogers@arcadia-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T16:15:00Z
Subject: Follow-up + DPA clarifications from today's call

Hi Diane -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our discovery call:

- Key objectives: Evaluate Redwood for secure, low-latency inference across patient-facing workflows (PHI-light but still sensitive PII).
- Primary requirements you flagged: data residency in US, 90-day retention for raw logs, SOC 2 + annual pen testing evidence, and explicit breach notification SLA.
- Action items: I will share a concise DPA summary addressing controller/processor roles, subprocessors, breach notice timelines, and logging/retention controls. Your legal team will send any initial redlines.

Attached is a short DPA summary that maps our standard positions to the specific items you raised (see attachment: Redwood_DPA_Summary_20270422.pdf). A few notes up front:

1) Roles: Redwood acts as Processor for customer-supplied data; Arcadia Health remains the Controller. We are open to discussing contract language to reflect that.
2) Subprocessors: We provide a current subprocessors list and commit to 30 days notice prior to adding new subprocessors.
3) Breach notice: Our standard is to notify customers within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that impacts customer data, and to provide regular updates.
4) Data residency: We can commit to US-only processing and storage for your tenant if agreed in contract and deployed to our US-only Dedicated/Private environment.
5) Logging & retention: We offer configurable retention windows; default production logs (non-KV inference telemetry) retained 90 days, full request logs (including prompt text) can be configured shorter; we support token-level redaction upon request for regulated workflows.

Next steps:
- I attached the DPA summary for your legal team to review.
- If you can send any initial redlines (ARC-DPA-redlines.docx) we'll review internally and loop in our legal/compliance.
- Dev can set up a short technical session on our logging/retention controls early next week if helpful.

Thanks - happy to hop on a call with your legal lead if that speeds things up.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0131

Attachment(s): Redwood_DPA_Summary_20270422.pdf
From: Diane Rogers <diane.rogers@arcadia-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@arcadia-health.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up + DPA clarifications from today's call

Hi Marissa - thanks for the quick recap and doc. Our legal team had a few clarifying questions after a first pass:

1) Controller vs Processor: We understand Redwood positions as Processor. Our standard DPA has a few paragraphs that reference joint controller language for certain data enrichment activities. Can you confirm Redwood would not assert any controller rights over customer data and that the DPA will reflect Processor-only obligations?

2) Subprocessors: Please share the current list of subprocessors and confirm the 30-day notice mechanism - is that notification by email or posted to a public page? Will there be an approval process for critical subprocessors (e.g., cloud infra providers)?

3) Breach notice: 72 hours is a good starting point; however Arcadia requires an initial notification within 48 hours and daily updates until resolution for incidents affecting PHI/PII. Can Redwood accommodate that timeline and provide a primary incident contact and escalation path?

4) Data residency & export: We need contractual guarantees that data will be stored and processed in US-only infrastructure for Arcadia. If Redwood relies on any global backups or replication, we need to understand where those are located and whether we can opt-out.

5) Logs & retention: We want clearer definitions of the different log types (audit logs, inference request logs, aggregated telemetry). Can you provide:
   - Which logs include unredacted prompt text?
   - Options to truncate or redact PII from logs automatically?
   - The mechanism for a customer to request deletion of stored prompts and associated KV caches.

We may send a redline of your standard DPA (we've put a placeholder in the attached ARC-DPA-redlines.docx). Please loop in your security/compliance contact and Dev for the technical clarifications.

Thanks,
Diane
Director of Product Security | Arcadia Health
Diane.Rogers@arcadia-health.com

Subject: Re: DPA clarifications - Arcadia Health

Hi Diane / Arcadia Legal -

Thanks for the detailed questions. Looping in Ben (Head of Compliance) and Dev for the technical bits - see responses below and attached updated DPA summary that calls out the items you raised (attachment: Redwood_DPA_Summary_20270422.pdf). If helpful, Ben is available Thurs afternoon for a legal-to-legal sync.

Responses (high level):

1) Controller vs Processor
- Confirmed: Redwood will sign DPA language reflecting Processor-only status. We will not claim Controller rights over customer data in standard onboarding or in the DPA.

2) Subprocessors
- Current subprocessors: AWS (us-east-1) for infrastructure, FastCache Inc. for managed caching, and LogStream Solutions for aggregated telemetry. Full list attached in the DPA summary.
- Notice: We maintain a public subprocessors page and will email contractual contacts for customers with Dedicated/Private deployments. The 30-day notice is by email to the technical/legal contact on file; customers on Dedicated can request manual approval workflows.

3) Breach notice and incident response
- We can accommodate a 48-hour initial notification for Arcadia and agree to daily status updates until containment/resolution. Our incident response process includes a named incident lead and a dedicated escalation channel; we'll provide that contact once mutual NDA/DPA are in place.

4) Data residency & backups
- For US-only commitment: we can guarantee US-only processing and storage when Arcadia is onboarded to our US-only Dedicated or Private deployment. We do not mirror production data to other regions by default.
- Global backups: Our hosted tenants may have cross-region backups unless contractually restricted; for Arcadia we can gate replication to US regions only as part of the Dedicated/Private contract.

5) Logs & retention
- Definitions: audit logs (user/admin actions, retained 1 year by default), inference request logs (may contain prompt text - default retention 90 days), aggregated telemetry (non-identifying performance metrics).
- Prompt text: inference request logs include unredacted prompt text by default. We offer an option to redact prompts at ingestion or to configure automatic truncation.
- Deletion requests: we support on-demand deletion of stored prompts and KV caches; Dev will follow up with the API/operational steps and timelines (we typically honor deletion within 7 business days for production tenants).

Next steps:
- Attached: Redwood_DPA_Summary_20270422.pdf (updated) and a link to our subprocessors page.
- Please send any redlines; Ben can review and propose contract language.
- Dev to propose a short technical session next week to demo log redaction options and the deletion API.

Ben & Dev - can you confirm the 7-business-day deletion SLA for production KV caches and provide the subprocessors page link in reply?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0131
